145688.title: fix(agents): run tool code child with Node under Bun
145688.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Bun cannot run `tool_search_code` because the sandboxed code child requires Node's `--permission` flag. The runtime checked Bun's own flags and launched `process.execPath`, so a direct-Bun MCP recovery test failed before the code child started.

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw now resolves a real Node executable for runtime-specific sidecars. The resolver walks `PATH` plus stable system locations, skips Bun's optional `node` shim, verifies the requested Node flag in a sterile probe process, and caches the result by runtime and executable-search inputs. Tool Search uses that verified Node for its isolated child and advertises code mode under Bun only when a compatible Node is available. The existing test Node resolver now shares the same owner.

## User Impact

Bun-hosted OpenClaw can use the full sandboxed Tool Search code mode while Node behavior stays unchanged. This adds no dependency and does not alter Node installation or package-manager behavior; it only locates an already-installed compatible Node for the child process. Electron keeps its existing structured-tool fallback.

## Evidence

- Direct custom Bun: Tool Search MCP recovery 8/8 passed; before the fix the code-mode case failed with the Node `--permission` runtime error.
- Direct custom Bun: full focused Tool Search and child lifecycle set 204/204 passed, plus the Node resolver regression 1/1.
- Node: the same focused matrix passed 213/213.
- Bun config smoke resolves code mode in about 47 ms on the first probe and 0.02 ms from cache.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: passed.
- Test-audit: the existing shim regression protects runtime identity, the credible regression is a Bun shim being selected as Node, and the refactor adds no test-only production seam or duplicate test.
- Independent P0-P2 autoreview: scoped clean at 0.89 confidence.

146616.title: fix: preserve custom-plugin sibling imports during updates
146616.body:
Closes #146609

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes custom plugins failing to load during update rehearsal when their runtime or Doctor entry imports shared source outside the plugin directory.

## User Impact

Enabled custom plugins keep their statically resolvable sibling imports in the private update snapshot. Candidate Doctor also completes copies made by the already-published 2026.9.4 updater, so the first upgrade can benefit from the fix. Original plugin files and configuration remain unchanged.

Recovery of old snapshots requires a recognized external-path projection and matching source/manifest bytes. Older managed-state or cross-volume projections that lost their original path produce diagnostics. Arbitrarily computed module paths are outside static dependency discovery; explicit external absolute imports retain their existing semantics.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the plugin source-capture owner to identify literal imports, CommonJS requires, package-map references, and linked workspace dependencies without evaluating plugin code. Feed those inputs into the existing measured private-copy planner.

Before candidate Doctor executes plugin repair hooks, complete only missing files in recognized published-driver snapshots. The same entry selection, source inspection, and copy owner serve both update paths, with source freshness and private-path validation. Complete snapshots continue working without the original source tree.

Reported by Jenna Brinning: https://x.com/jennabrinning/status/2098875692691677271

## Evidence

The final package rerun passed, including the optional-import correction, against commit `5a5d6149901d3d2c99480816f74af4cd88e9b3b8`. Candidate tarball SHA256: `e562553dadf9edd32ba6917410d6495ee390ab4893da4d91ebca12e248d0624b`. The [Testbox run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34730198942) completed its delegated command with exit 0: four private plugin executions, both source URLs private, update success, original hashes and enablement preserved. Linux Docker proof uses the published 2026.9.4 updater against packages produced by the canonical candidate builder. The sibling-import scenario fails on the pre-fix candidate; changing only the helper location/import to a self-contained control passes. The fixed candidate passes with actual Doctor callbacks and Gateway canary registration, private plugin and dependency URLs, unchanged original source hashes, preserved enablement, and successful runtime inspection before and after update.

Focused source tests reproduce the missing-file failure before the fix and execute copied plugins after the original tree is removed. Coverage includes directory/file locators, imports, CommonJS subpaths, literal dynamic imports, package maps, linked dependencies, optional imports, old-driver repair, source changes, authority revocation, and private symlink escapes. The latest focused suites pass 8 source-copy cases and 27 repair cases; 67 Doctor preflight cases and the full changed-file gate also passed. Final type and lint checks cover the subsequent optional-import correction. Independent review checks the production boundary through P2.

149520.title: fix: reduce memory use in long-running Codex sessions
149520.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes excessive gateway heap use when long-running Codex sessions load their entire mirrored history for prompt and compaction hooks.

## User Impact

Codex hook context stays bounded as stored history grows. The latest complete tool frame and compaction/reset boundary are retained. If required context cannot fit, the read fails explicitly instead of continuing with empty history. An authorized standalone `/reset` or `/new` clears active context so bounded reads can proceed. This is an explicit loss of active conversation continuity, not an automatic reset. `/reset soft` does not recover this condition. The bounded reader leaves full transcripts and native Codex resume state intact.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SQLite model-context reader now selects a bounded recent context before message bodies enter JavaScript or cross the worker boundary. Codex uses its effective context budget for these reads. Optional SDK limits preserve existing behavior for other callers.

## Evidence

A synthetic reproduction uses the real Codex history reader and an authorized prompt hook with 5,001 messages. The unmodified base returns 31,022,852 bytes and the hook clone adds 21,210,936 heap bytes. The patched reader returns 1,005,282 bytes and the hook clone adds 745,368 heap bytes. The newest message survives and stored transcript hashes remain identical.

The measured allocation path matches the observed structured-clone heap failure, but this is isolated source-runtime proof, not a production memory measurement or proof that every historical crash had the same caller. This change does not add automatic resumption of interrupted runs.

Validation: 99 focused model-context/history tests and 322 surrounding Codex integration tests pass. Independent source-blind probes cover bounded tails, summaries, tool ownership, private-field exclusion, empty histories, and invalid limits; the initial empty-history finding is fixed and all eight follow-up probes pass.

Repository changed-file checks and final independent autoreview also pass.

152758.title: feat(ui): preview ordinary external links on hover
152758.body:
Closes #152442

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Web UI links give little context before opening another tab, unlike specialized GitHub previews.

## User Impact

Hover or keyboard-focus an ordinary external link to see its favicon, social image, title, and description. Keyboard navigation, Escape, touch navigation, and text-only fallbacks remain usable.

The existing automatic-favicon opt-out disables this enrichment. When enabled, deliberate hover or focus sends the eligible URL—including path and query—to the Gateway for bounded anonymous fetching; browser cookies and site credentials are not forwarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing link-reader hover owner now presents ordinary page metadata alongside plugin previews, rather than introducing a competing hover provider. Plugin claims—including detail-only links—retain priority, and ordinary links never enter transcript prefetch. Browser cards and ordinary hovers share the public metadata cache; plugin identity and recovery behavior stay separate.

165608.title: perf(gateway): acknowledge chat sends before skill preparation
165608.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`chat.send` waits for skill selection and authoring before acknowledging an admitted message, and slow-send logs cannot distinguish acknowledgement work from reply startup.

## User Impact

Durably admitted messages can be acknowledged before skill preparation finishes. The admitted run owns preparation, cancellation, and error publication. Receipt fields, input bytes, idempotency, and message order remain unchanged.

**The median-ACK performance target remains unmet.** The prior 100-send comparison measured ACK p50 **130.98 → 144.50 ms** and p99 **431.96 → 299.47 ms**, versus requested limits of 50/200 ms. First assistant delta p50/p99 improved **1488.70/4757.73 → 1416.39/2567.24 ms**. These are historical measurements, not measurements of the rebased head. The change provides post-ACK preparation and diagnostics; it does not establish a median improvement or explain the reported production three-second tail. No obvious source-level cause for the 13.52 ms median regression was established during the conflict repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move selection and authoring into existing detached dispatch. Reserve the existing reply-admission ticket before ACK and retain it across preparation and pre-execution retries, so later inputs cannot overtake stalled or retrying inputs. Current input authority is revalidated before startup and retries; accepted injection keeps its existing backing-run outcome.

The timing owner emits `slow chat send <N>ms` request/startup records at one second and `openclaw_chat_send_phase_seconds{phase,stage}` with bounded labels. Initial session-row reads remain in `replyInitialization`, ordinary sandbox readiness remains in `preparation`, and `worktree` covers pending workspace creation. The optional transcript-start reader has a nested `snapshot` observation. Inclusive, overlapping phases must not be summed.

Rebased onto `876dd7520f7b4eb9a30933fbee90b173386ce540`. The sole textual conflict was the session-prepared callback: main's `replyDispatch.notePreparedSession(binding)` handoff remains alongside the phase mark. Timing accepts narrow input facts without importing the admission/request/session owners, removing the type-import cycle. The two stale tests now use the synchronous preparation result and wait for existing dispatch settlement before counting dispatches.

Production LOC is **+422 / −172, net +250**, excluding tests, test support, and docs. The repair itself removes three net lines. Growth in the overall feature is required for the new diagnostic lifecycle/histogram and FIFO ownership across deferred preparation and retries. Eager preparation paths and superseded timing helpers are removed. No new configuration, cache, protocol field, compatibility shim, or schema change is introduced. Release-note context is this description; the changelog is release-owned.

## Evidence

Final repair head `fcc8409858e1b755b19ddb35508513f91f1172d3` has tested tree `d1a61d996db2ff523309a25f8b80bf2a3f5f903b`. The media-path test still expected the former parked fallback. The unchanged base reproduced that exact failure. While the repair was being validated, main landed `50b3573d11ea` with the same fixture correction and a stronger exact-argument assertion. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Doctor/updater recovery copies miss Canvas legacy documents and Memory Core host-event and sidecar files when their state migrations then delete or move those originals.

Strict update/Doctor checks and recovery-generation inspection rewrote entire private SQLite snapshots, even when Btrfs could share unchanged storage.

A source replacement during guarded copy admission stops that snapshot rather than retrying: helper errors cannot safely distinguish source drift from simultaneous destination, I/O, or cleanup failure. Unambiguous source-only drift retains bounded retry.

173346.title: feat(claws): review selected private packages before publishing
173346.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A useful OpenClaw agent has no safe path to a shareable Claw: copying its workspace could expose private context, and a creator cannot verify the exact package before publication. This PR makes the agent write a bounded proposal, builds only selected portable files and declared dependencies, and requires an explicit human publish action under the creator’s ClawHub account. The privacy, selection, stale-review, publisher, authority, and upload tests pass (15/15).

## Summary

An agent can prepare a private, portable Claw proposal for human review. The bundled, manual-only `create-claw` skill keeps the chat command short and guides the agent to inspect its durable instructions and relevant Gateway capabilities. The Gateway builds the archive from authored proposal text, exposes its exact files and declared dependencies, and applies the creator's name, description, and checkbox exclusions before a fresh review token is issued. Only an explicit Publish uploads under the creator's personal ClawHub identity.

```text
agent-authored proposal → isolated package build → exact-file review → selected archive → explicit Publish
```

The source workspace is never copied wholesale. Known private paths and credential-like text are rejected; creators still inspect the complete archive for personal facts automated checks cannot recognize. Plugin and skill declarations are requirements, not copies of installed Gateway code.

## Evidence

- **Before:** The draft API exposed a raw proposal editor and could not remove individual files or dependencies from the reviewed package.
- **After:** `src/claws/draft.test.ts` proves unchecked files and dependencies are absent from the exact built archive, and the review token changes with the selection. Privacy, stale-review, publisher-change, authority, and single-upload tests pass (15/15).
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed. The manual skill is excluded from normal model invocation context and is invoked by the UI's explicit `/skill create-claw` message.
- Earlier local ClawHub integration established real auth, package storage, discovery, download, Add, and ordinary-agent chat with simulated external scanner receipts. The revised same-chat UI is in #173377; its new browser proof is separate and ongoing.

Depends on #173345 for consumer discovery and Add. ClawHub's community-discovery gate is in [ClawHub #3963](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3963).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** Two-way for code; publishing creates an immutable public package version. **Blast Radius:** Administrator Claws draft methods behind the Labs flag. A Gateway-host workspace and ClawHub login are currently required.

176001.body: ## What Problem This Solves After a local managed workspace accepts a refreshed upstream base, Review can include upstream-only changes when the checkout's shared default-branch refs still point to an older commit. ## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Claude CLI turns losing a nested background agent's forwarded answer when its launching subagent finishes first, while preserving the fix for turns hanging when that subagent consumes the answer itself.

## User Impact

The outer reply stays interim until Claude returns the forwarded child answer. If the running subagent consumes its child's result, the parent's final answer finishes normally. Completed turns can reuse their warm process; surviving foreground descendants still retire with that process and cannot borrow a later turn's permissions.

Current main excludes every task with a parent ID from input ownership. The integration reuses one tracker and removes the proposed parallel running-task map. Task-event bookkeeping lives with the existing task ownership helpers; permission checks, settlement, and process retirement remain in the runtime. Main's foreground-descendant safeguard and prior-input isolation stay covered. The existing Agent/Workflow regression now covers both completion orders rather than adding a duplicate fixture. 186288.title: fix(agents): avoid oversized raw history in final answers
186288.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Isolated post-tool finalization reopened raw session history even when the selected context engine had already excluded that history from the source attempt. A short final answer could therefore send a much larger conversation to the provider.

Fixes #186244. Already-delivered-message admission is tracked separately in #179003 and is outside this repair, as [confirmed by the maintainer](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186288#issuecomment-6454269644).

## Why This Change Was Made

The restricted built-in adapter passes the frozen settled model view through a host-private parameter. It uses the explicit OpenClaw transcript capture when present, otherwise the canonical settled `messagesSnapshot`; an explicitly unavailable or foreign-harness projection is refused.

The existing `prepareEmbeddedAttemptHistory` owner selects this view instead of rehydrated raw history and reuses the existing session byte/event window and tool-result omission policy. An empty selected view also replaces the hydrated messages. The original SessionManager retains all transcript writes and receipts.

The finalizer still receives no live context engine. Its bootstrap, maintenance, ingestion, afterTurn hooks, ambient prompt contributors, tools and trajectory capabilities are not restored. Empty-finalizer retries reuse the original settled view. This adds no config/env/schema or public SDK capability and introduces no new current-turn boundary inference.

## User Impact

Excluded old history stays out of the isolated finalization request while the current request, completed tool evidence and selected summary remain available. Durable history is retained. Finalization remains tool-free, and interrupted work cannot be completed by replaying tools during this step.

## Evidence

### Refreshed main integration

Merged main `342da13c92e0af1add7936f9bc479394f01e426c` into the latest contributor head, producing `a8cad32e618122fbe474a5102890fe34e5fc9b57`. The history owner preserves both main's Anthropic turn-scoped system-update clearing and the frozen selected-view snapshot. [Fresh built-Gateway proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186288#issuecomment-6456933305) measured one finalizer request per ref: **52,085 bytes on main** (excluded raw canary restored) versus **2,490 bytes on the merged candidate** (summary and current write receipt retained, canary absent). Both turns completed successfully, offered zero finalizer tools, and added no engine lifecycle calls. The 11 finalization tests and 8 upstream bounded-context tests passed again, with focused lint/formatting. Test-line growth remains zero.

### Independent current-main comparison

[Independent built-Gateway evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186288#issuecomment-6456615096) compares current main `4b27ee88cec9a78377a04b2e3a352ba7c503450e` twice with the candidate production code twice, plus normal-finalization controls on both revisions. Isolated finalizer requests measured **52,100 bytes on main in both runs** versus **2,505 bytes on the candidate in both runs**. Main restored the excluded raw canary; the candidate retained the selected summary and current write receipt without the canary. Every isolated finalizer offered zero tools and left context-engine lifecycle counters unchanged. All six measured turns completed successfully. The latest contributor head changes only tests and passed both changed suites (11 tests), focused lint and formatting. Whole-PR test-line delta is zero, without a ceiling change.

### Contributor's earlier proof

Named base: `63ba4974f67c1eba483f8b7121c2bf7416d75ae4`.

Candidate: `a037f29b1bad9717aca3a3db9559b941534e4efd`.

### Real built CLI/Gateway proof on Linux

Both revisions completed frozen dependency installation and full builds. Final candidate full build exited 0 in 3m2.2s; the actual built CLI reported `OpenClaw 2026.10.7 (a037f29)`.

The primary fixture uses a real Gateway, `sessions.create`, two agent CLI turns and an actual committed `write` to a task-owned file. 189847.title: improve(ui): make spinners fuller
189847.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running-session spinners read thin: a short arc with sharp ends on a pale track, drawn with a different arc and stroke on almost every surface.

## User Impact

Spinners across the Control UI now share one shape: a closed ring at 20% with a short solid arc with round ends. Sizes, layout boxes and each spinner's rotation speed are unchanged, so rows do not move.

## Why This Change Was Made

Spinners had drifted to different arcs and strokes from 1 to 2.5px. They now share one set of mask tokens in `base.css`.

- **Shape:** a border cannot round its ends, so each spinner masks `currentColor` with an SVG: a ring at 20% and an arc of 26% of the circumference. The ring and arc follow the surrounding color, and rotation stays a transform.
- **Stroke:** the SVG sizes itself to the element, so a stroke stays the same px at any size. 2px by default, 1.5px on 8 to 9px badges, 1.75px on the 24px avatar ring and the pair trace, 2.5px on panel, approval, config and sign-in rings.
- **Pair trace:** the same recipe, with its track now visible at 20%.
- **Reduced motion:** the mask becomes the closed ring at full strength, so a still spinner never reads as a frozen arc.
- **Forced colors:** the masks show through a background that forced colors would repaint, so spinners opt out and paint `CanvasText`.
- **Color:** progress, automation and custodian history spinners use the accent. Spinners inside buttons, and the Gateway reconnect status, keep their surrounding color.
- **Background work** keeps its 60% opacity.
- **Avatar badges in the processes and subagents panels** keep their opaque disc, so the mask sits on a pseudo-element there.

Lucide icons that spin (refresh, loader) are a different look and are unchanged.

## Evidence

All states come from the mock data layer with real components. The image is from the commit before the head, which only restores durations.

**Before and after, sidebar rows, Absolutely dark** (Chromium)

![Before and after, sidebar rows, Absolutely dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ddd4f042-12d4-4dbe-8473-dd17343dcfa2)

**After, Absolutely dark** (Chromium, browser zoom 2x on the sidebar, at the head)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ef3a3ff-db0b-4c1a-86b4-513fb42f9b9d

Real Safari 27.0.1 was also checked: the masks render, with round ends and a visible track in light.

**Behavior and checks**

- No `animation` or duration line differs from the base across the changed CSS.
- With 6 spinners over 15 seconds idle, plus row hover, session switching and scrolling: no spinner remounts and no animation restarts (Chromium).
- The pair trace animates `stroke-dashoffset` on the main thread, so it freezes during a blocked main thread and costs about 60 style recalculations and 180 paints per second for 2 rows. This predates the change and is not addressed here.
- stylelint, oxfmt, oxlint, `tsgo:ui`, the spinner unit, browser and E2E tests and `ui:check-performance:base` pass.

**Not verified:** in real Safari, the goal resume spinners and custodian history were not reached through the mock. Forced colors and reduced motion were checked in Chromium emulation only. No capture was taken on a 1x display.


High-contrast accessibility: the Processes and Subagents badge keeps its opaque backing under the browser’s forced-color mapping; only the masked ring opts out. A focused regression fails on the prior CSS and passes with the repair. Existing glyph and forced-color checks pass (9 tests). Assertions tied to exact SVG arc and stroke serialization were removed.

190223.title: fix: prepared PRs cannot refresh their target branch
190223.body: Fixes #190201. ## What Problem This Solves A guest who recovered an existing PR with `prepare_pr` could publish further changes, then become unable to integrate the target branch. `refresh_base` rejected every associated PR and redirected back to preparation, which updates PR source and review comparison without merging destination-only changes. ## User Impact Prepared and recovered PRs can integrate their current target branch, resolve conflicts, and continue publishing to the original PR. Saved guest files and Git history remain intact. Distinct staged and unstaged versions are preserved by refusing the refresh until the staged work is committed; existing requester permissions and changed-remote-head publication checks remain in effect. ## Why This Change Was Made Bound base refresh now uses the existing PR preparation owner to verify the current requester, publisher, PR identity, and target, then passes that verified base to the existing workspace integration owner. It keeps accepted PR-head metadata separate from the target being merged. Pending head preparation and pending base integration remain separate operations, and a retry finishes its accepted base before selecting another target. A previous publication still identifies the accepted head after the PR is retargeted; it is matched by its original head branch rather than its former target branch. Review comparison follows the integrated host history, so repeating preparation does not discard a completed base merge from the comparison. No configuration, schema, or public action parameters are added. ## Evidence The registered-action regression first reproduced the original refusal after outside head advancement, successful preparation, and same-PR publication, with both linked and unlinked guests. They use real authorization/Git/storage owners with fixed external GitHub/container I/O; no live private-repository or exhaustive revocation claim is made. - Format/lint and the selected type families passed again for the test-only addition. 191711.title: fix(sessions): attribute and reduce slow cron transcript hydration
191711.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived cron sessions with many background results can spend seconds hydrating a small model-context window. Existing slow-hold logs report inclusive callback time as `sqlMs`, so they cannot distinguish statement execution from work between statements. Related: #191236.

## User Impact

Hydration avoids repeated navigation projection while preserving pending results across compaction, native exclusion of unrelated payloads, and the coherent read snapshot. Slow hydration warnings gain bounded statement and GC attribution without a new log stream or configuration. Production causality still needs confirmation from the next deployment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Dependency predicates expand the same guarded navigation expression repeatedly. One materialized CTE evaluates it once; the existing predicates and exact payload lookups consume that result. A native evaluation regression proves seven projections become one. This also removes an intermediate candidate mapping. No schema, index, persistent table, or cache changes.

The existing statement timer now recognizes inherited `sessions.transcript-hydration.*` labels. It reports five ranked groups, returned/consumed rows, total native-call time, remaining callback wall time, and callback GC time; thread identity precedes large metadata. SQL and bindings remain absent. GC overlaps the wall timings and cannot be assigned to an individual statement.

## Evidence

Committed reproduction: `scripts/perf/cron-hydration-statement-measure.ts`. A synthetic 378.6 MB database has 5,000 sessions and 1k/10k/50k background-heavy, ordinary, and excluded-user histories. Fixed 50-event/1,024,000-byte selection; pending results survive compaction. Five counterbalanced process pairs contain A/A controls (10 samples per cell), separate allocation/profile runs, and matching returned-event digests. Timing/allocation below disable the diagnostic-channel observer; native statements were measured separately. macOS/APFS, Node 26.12.1, SQLite 3.54.1; warm/uncontrolled OS cache.

| 50k background history | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Owner wall median / p95 | 1,466 / 2,327 ms | 364 / 587 ms |
| Thread CPU median | 1,460 ms | 362 ms |
| Sampled JS allocation | 58.39 MiB | 42.30 MiB |
| Native dependency query | 1,405 ms | 325 ms |
| Process peak RSS | 446.68 MiB | 477.59 MiB |

The explicit tradeoff is +6.9% peak process RSS (including runtime/native memory) for about 75% less wall/CPU time; no retained cache is introduced. Ordinary and excluded-user controls improve too. A/A background wall medians are 1,466/1,467 ms before and 363/366 ms after. Payload selection remains about 0.16–0.17 ms with 65 returned events. History discovery remains linear where pending-result semantics require it; this is not an O(context-window) claim. These are owner measurements, not whole-Gateway or production latency.

Validation: 26 hydration/query tests, 21 transaction/observation tests, one Chromium history-settlement browser test, and nine built-UI messaging E2E tests pass. The native projection regression fails on the base (7 vs expected 1); hydration attribution also fails on the base and passes after. Real forced GC is reported, then excluded from the next callback. Typechecks, lint, formatting, import/schema/worker guards, unused-file checks, and zero-net-growth test budget pass. Net production growth is 72 lines (62 attribution, 10 query repair); test growth is zero.

`pnpm check:changed` completes with one inherited failure category: five unused exports from #191665 (`a5eb424e6347`). The identical five findings reproduce on exact main parent `f107fd67bfee`; the affected owners are unchanged. This is a main regression requiring follow-up, not a green aggregate check. No baseline or ignore exception is added.

Independent Codex autoreview covers the full candidate against `f107fd67bfee` through P2; result: scoped-clean, no accepted/actionable P0–P2 findings. The 26 owner tests take 36.49 seconds including existing native-history coverage; diagnostic tests take 0.73 seconds. Browser/E2E proof takes 3.34/34.16 seconds respectively (E2E includes production build).

192766.title: fix(ui): turn Skill Workshop on from its page when its plugin is off
192766.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI shows a broken Skill Workshop when the skill-workshop plugin is turned off or missing. Opening the page showed "Could not load the Workshop. unknown method: skills.workshop.list" with a Retry button that could never succeed. Separately, upgraded installs with a `plugins.allow` list written while the Workshop was built in would lose the Workshop, because the new plugin was not on their list.

## User Impact

- With the plugin enabled (the default), nothing changes.
- When the plugin is off, the Workshop page says "Skill Workshop is off" and shows a **Turn on Skill Workshop** button. One click turns the plugin on and the page loads the Workshop in place, with no reload.

195661.title: fix(sessions): preserve yielded roots across Gateway restarts
195661.body:
Related: #195387, #195420

## What Problem This Solves

Dashboard/operator roots parked in `sessions_yield` could lose their lifecycle during Gateway restart. Separately, permanently rejected child-result handoff could retire the completion batch while leaving its yielded requester active indefinitely.

## User Impact

A reachable recorded yield wait remains parked without a startup model turn. When restart stops the requester's own child executions, the root receives its ordinary recovery input to reconcile their work; it does not wait for those old executions or fail merely because they stopped. A truly unavailable external continuation source closes with a visible recorded outcome.

Permanent handoff failure now uses the existing classified run-failure notice: the child result could not be delivered, the conversation is preserved, and the user should inspect saved child work and retry or resend. Stop, reset and newer turns retain ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

The registry's existing requester/cohort index supplies shutdown candidates and distinguishes reachable waits from stopped descendants requiring root reconciliation. Startup uses that distinction without restoring old execution authority. A mixed cohort needing reconciliation takes the root recovery path. Persisted `createdVia: "spawn"` keeps dashboard-key children with their requester at marking and startup; stale registry records cannot redirect an ordinary conversation. Children are not independently replayed. The truly ownerless mid-turn orphan branch remains. Shared-database recovery waits for the session’s logical agent through the existing admission owner before consuming its marker; cohort classification uses that same logical identity.

The durable completion owner retains the original requester run identity, settles only that yielded lifecycle on permanent delivery failure, and retries observed settlement bookkeeping without replaying delivery. Stable batches did not persist that ID. Their failed handoffs record the same classified notice under the existing batch identity, using their recorded physical store, without guessing which current lifecycle they own. A replacement writer remains untouched; no session read or history scan is added. No schema, migration, configuration or cache is added. Production growth is **270 lines** against `85307438e998`, justified by dependency classification and exact lifecycle settlement; the existing receipt map moves to its mutation owner rather than being duplicated. The exact regression-test allocation is **502 lines**.

Integration: #195420 overlaps the sweep-settle helper and yielded-settlement test table. Preserve its committed-requester check and live-notice case when combining; this PR does not duplicate its listener fix. #194732 removes completion-authority bookkeeping, including the current-main `isCompletionAuthorityRetired` API used by wait classification here; reconcile that boundary when combining those branches. #195275 changes the adjacent admitted wake path without a direct file overlap. #192845 separately owns fallback after an admitted requester stalls.

## Evidence

Rebased after #195773 and #195754 landed. Shutdown selection retains restart-aborted preparing turns, user/completed-turn exclusions, and parked-wait enumeration. Both adjacent regression groups remain. The documentation describes both behaviors. Main's dispatch/admission changes and selector grouping cleanup stay intact. Range-diff confirms the second repair commit is patch-identical.

Validated head: `f28256354ea6ed08ea73cbedf8ac60dede2243d7`, rebased onto `85307438e9982b9133a0960b78f837bfbf3e6f4c`. Not merged.

The original head `b6376657406a` failed the existing `gateway-restart-resume.e2e.test.ts` expectation `RESUMED_0_parent`. That test and expectation remain unchanged and now pass. Before-fix regressions also showed generic handoff-failure copy, a legacy batch terminating a replacement writer, and missing legacy notices when the recorded physical store path was omitted. The final implementation fixes each at its owner boundary. The handoff failure reproduces a lifecycle leak; it does not establish the exact historical cause of the reported idle run.

Latest stable is [v2026.11.2](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.2), commit `b556fdf457b0`. The upgrade cases seed literal session/registry JSON matching its writers, including the private completion envelope, with no `resumeAfterRestart` or new requester run field. They load through the real SQLite registry loader and session reader: a message-waiting child keeps its root parked, and an interrupted child triggers exactly one root recovery across repeated startup. A shared-store case separates the physical owner from the logical requester. Receipt cases cover stable permanent rejection, notice persistence retry, and replacement writers both before and during handoff. Legacy notices preserve the current lifecycle because the stored record cannot prove its original writer. This proves stored-record compatibility, not a full historical-binary installation.

Validation on the rebased source: **147 focused tests passed**, including restart/upgrade/prestart/lifecycle owners, ACP abort, admission waiting, yielded settlement, failure copy and all requester receipt cases. **All five selected real Gateway restart scenarios passed** (176.72 seconds), including the unchanged original E2E and dashboard reconciliation without child replay; three unrelated scenarios were unselected. Runtime build and fresh Codex autoreview through P2 pass. Required UI proof from the preceding repair passed three browser and seven UI E2E tests; no UI-facing patch changed during conflict resolution. The test-line command `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base origin/main --no-merge-base` passes: this PR adds exactly 502 lines and main retains its pre-existing seven lines of slack. Full changed checks pinned to `85307438e998` passed all code gates. Their sole red remains 20 historical changelog attributions, reproduced from that exact parent's immutable checker/data blobs and introduced by `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957` / #194364. This is a main regression for the release owner, not a green check or ignored noise. Local default Bun attempts exposed a separate macOS native watcher shutdown stall; the existing nonblocking watcher helper excludes Bun. A minimal candidate was investigated but is outside this PR because its native-event tests need a separate reliable fixture repair. Final Gateway proof uses the repository's CI Node runtime, with the original test and its deadlines unchanged. The Bun failures are retained as a follow-up, not claimed as an inherited CI waiver.

Prior-head owner measurements used a synthetic 35.129 GiB, 10,000-session, one-million-event fixture with counterbalanced A/B and A/A controls. Four extra root markers added 8.64 ms shutdown wall time, 10.72 ms process CPU and 333 kB sampled host allocation; worker tasks remained one per shutdown and ten per startup. These are retained measurements of the earlier head, not fresh measurements of this repair. No startup speedup or btrfs result is claimed. No production data or Team access.

196662.title: fix(sandbox): resume btrfs workspaces after atomic checkpoint capture
196662.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Changed sandbox commands freeze the guest throughout workspace discovery, Git capture, and canonical reconciliation. With large workspaces, scanning alone can take seconds while every process in the container is paused.

## User Impact

For provisioned btrfs subvolumes, checkpoint now pauses for the existing native snapshot operation, resumes the guest, and synchronizes canonical state from that captured tree. Command completion still waits for canonical acceptance, preserving read-after-command consistency. Initial recovery and imports retain their existing pause boundaries. No configuration, schema, dependency, or cache is added.

## Why This Change Was Made

The checkpoint owner reuses the template backend's native copy primitive under its existing lease. Snapshot fingerprints translate only the proven snapshot device back to the source identity, preserving unchanged probes. Btrfs omits nested subvolumes: the manifest walker detects its inode-2 placeholders before accepting a receipt, then re-pauses under the same lease and uses the existing complete Git capture. Unsupported backends and ordinary directories also retain that path, resuming after durable capture.

The owner removes its private capture after resume and removes leftovers on the next lease. Native removal now repairs inaccessible directories only after a permission failure; it does not follow symlinks or change live source permissions. This is required for snapshots containing ordinary read-only workspace directories.

Snapshot creation can wait for btrfs dirty-data writeback, so this bounds the paused work rather than promising a fixed wall-clock limit. Recursive snapshot cleanup adds work after resume; the native comparison will report that cost explicitly.

## Evidence

The real Podman+btrfs comparison completed all five counterbalanced pairs: 50 measured mutating commands per arm, plus two A/A controls. Every command passed canonical and subsequent guest read checks. The fixture contains 62,000 synthetic files / 1.1 GB, 10,001 session metadata rows, and a 33.65 GiB synthetic database. No production data was used.

| Metric | Parent | Atomic capture |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Pause p50 / p95 / max | 1,619.63 / 1,830.52 / 4,497.19 ms | 194.23 / 241.48 / 269.72 ms |
| Command p50 / p95 / max | 2,374.14 / 2,854.99 / 7,252.07 ms | 3,038.07 / 3,665.20 / 4,221.59 ms |
| Whole-cgroup CPU per command | 3,493.06 ms | 4,472.75 ms |
| Main-isolate allocation per command | 19.22 MB | 20.49 MB |

Median pause improves 88%; median command latency and whole-cgroup CPU increase 28%. A/A pause, command and CPU spread was about 1–1.3%; allocation spread was 9.4%, so no allocation benefit is claimed. All pairs, including the slower first candidate arm, are retained. The 1.36–1.42 s manifest scan runs paused on the parent and unpaused on the candidate in all 50 commands. Native snapshot copy takes 106 ms median; recursive cleanup takes 511 ms after resume. Cleanup explains most of the extra command latency. The maximum guest heartbeat gap falls from 4.43 s to 243 ms.

200758.title: fix: highlight the message box when dropping images into a new session
200758.body:

Fixes: dragging an image onto the New Session composer highlights the context tray underneath the message box instead of the message box itself.

## User Impact

User impact: the drop highlight now identifies the message surface where the image will be attached. Attachment admission, the shell-wide drop target, and draft text remain unchanged. No migration or user action is required.

200784.title: fix: update bundled Codex for newer ChatGPT models
200784.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native Codex model discovery uses the Codex client version. The bundled 0.164.0 runtime is behind the 0.169.0 CLI that @VACInc reports can see `gpt-6.2-sol` and `gpt-6.2-astra`. This updates the bundled runtime and matching protocol so the old native client does not hold back discovery.

Related: #200766 supplied the GPT-6.2 catalog and provider-transport support. Ben’s #197768 supplied native catalog forwarding through the inference relay and is now merged as [ed3230dd29d1](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ed3230dd29d1e162d814e38eff00f64dc77af64e). This PR includes that commit as an ancestor: it no longer contains the relay production changes and retains additional native-discovery and cleanup regression tests. It also preserves the subsequently merged #200811: the subscription picker independently requests `client_version=99.0.0`, while native app-server discovery still uses its actual binary version. The remaining OpenAI version fallback applies to Platform access-program discovery. These are complementary paths; actual native availability still depends on the account and backend.

## User Impact

Bundled Codex and the Platform access-program version fallback report version 0.169.0. Matching protocol validation accepts uploaded audio-file references without dropping a completed turn. This does not add GPT-6.2 catalog entries, change default models, or change authentication policy.

**Context limits stay unchanged:** the merged GPT-6.2 catalog records a 1,050,000-token model window, a 272,000-token default working budget, and a 128,000-token maximum output for Astra and Sol. User-selected limits and native context reporting remain unchanged. No files overlap the catalog/transport changes from #200766.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Update the package, lockfile, existing ACP version-parity override, runtime constant, OpenAI discovery fallback and documented version to 0.169.0.
- Regenerate the selected upstream schemas and standalone validators from `rust-v0.169.0`, using the existing repository generator helpers.
- Protect failed-turn settlement and visible errors for `modelNotFound`, `policyCapacityUnavailable` and `inferenceHookDenied`, including completed snapshots containing the new audio `fileId` representation.
- Recognize the new native `execve` launch diagnostic only when its path matches the native binary. Repair an HTTP test fixture that dropped shell arguments; production cleanup and permissions are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Protocol compatibility and generation provenance</summary>

No client request methods were removed. Selected response roots retain their required fields; dynamic-tool call parameters and model-list responses are unchanged. Optional item timestamps, agent-message moderation, image generation IDs and thread attachment IDs require no consumer change. The regenerated mirror includes Account’s `gcp` variant, optional ChatGPT `workspaceName` and optional GetAccountResponse `userId`, without enabling new authentication behavior. Optional `ModelListParams.modelProvider` remains omitted to use the configured provider. New memory, guardian, approved-plan, provider/GCP/account/security setup methods are not called. Audio URL and uploaded-file variants both validate.

Source: [rust-v0.169.0](https://github.com/openai/codex/tree/d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4/codex-rs/app-server-protocol/schema), commit `d32063f96c2dff1dc96af839b3952abb6acfeda4`. Used the checked-in experimental export archive with existing materialization, staging, compaction and formatting helpers, then `scripts/generate-codex-validators.mts`. All eight selected JSON schemas round-trip to those exports. No generated schema or validator was hand-edited. Rust/Cargo is unavailable here, so the Rust fixture compilation stage of `protocol:sync` was not rerun.

</details>

## Evidence

After rebasing onto Ben’s landed repair, focused protocol, failed-turn, terminal-error, HTTP-relay and native-binary tests passed: **94 passed, 1 optional live test skipped** across five files. The relay conflict retained 0.169.0 and the additional disconnect/shutdown regressions. The subsequent #200811 conflict retains the new broad subscription-picker test and removes this PR’s now-obsolete picker-version expectation. Codex and dependency file contents remain byte-identical to the tested candidate. After integrating #200811, the subscription-discovery, provider, Platform access-program and version-contract tests passed. Formatting and `git diff --check` passed.

An independent **P0–P3 review of the complete candidate after the relay rebase** returned `scoped-clean` with no actionable findings. That evidence is retained for the unchanged Codex/dependency delta; the later integration only removes an obsolete picker test and incorporates #200811’s existing behavior. No hostile behavior was identified in the reviewed delta; this is not an audit of all upstream dependency source.

The real pinned app-server requests its catalog through OpenClaw’s RPC client and loopback relay. Removing Ben’s repair causes 502 and no upstream request; restoring it returns a remote-only synthetic model through `model/list`, preserving native account headers. The external fetch boundary is mocked; separate real-HTTPS tests cover forwarding, auth separation, upstream errors and cleanup. Prior relay-family tests passed **88 tests**, with one optional live skip, plus extension-test typecheck and targeted type-aware lint.

Protocol-source/version contracts and affected OpenAI discovery/provider tests passed **68 tests**. Validator regeneration, targeted lint and the repaired HTTP fixture passed. Installed package reports `codex-cli 0.169.0`.

**Explicit base-fail/head-pass comparison:** the same failed-turn fixture with `codexErrorInfo: "modelNotFound"` and audio `{ "type": "audio", "fileId": "file-audio-1" }` was passed directly to the unchanged generated validators read from Git. Both `isCodexTurnCompletedNotification` and `isCodexTurnStartResponse` reject it at base `0a27bd7f85fa6af2964182a8c54a709b143fdefe` and accept it at published head `d2496ff4de05b0365d010783eea25b06affaaf3e`. The committed consumer regressions also pass on the head.

**Important scope of the regression:** new error-name strings alone already pass the old open-enum validator; the comparison confirms `modelNotFound` error notifications pass on both revisions. We do not claim those strings alone reproduced a hang. The concrete old-schema failure is a completed failed turn containing audio `fileId`; regeneration makes it validate and the tests protect error display and terminal settlement.

**Current-head hosted validation:** [CI run 44188975323](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44188975323) completed successfully for `d2496ff4de05b0365d010783eea25b06affaaf3e`. The remaining Apple checks also completed successfully, including [Periphery](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44188974909). At the final check, the only nonpassing statuses were `openclaw/dependency-review` and its combined `openclaw/ci-gate`: a repository admin or active SecOps member must approve this revision’s dependency change. This is not a claim that all required gates are green.

[ClawSweeper’s current-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200784#issuecomment-6960325018) reports no actionable code findings, confirms the runtime/protocol approach and resolved relay dependency, and retains the same approval gate. The PR remains open, with no auto-merge enabled.

<details>
<summary>Earlier validation and proof limitations</summary>

The initial full Codex suite ran 5,486 passing, 10 failing and 10 skipped tests. Focused follow-ups fixed all ten: version parity, the native launcher’s new diagnostic, dropped shell arguments in the HTTP fixture, and an isolated native test’s inherited certificate environment. Assertions, production permissions and timeouts were not weakened. A later audio-fixture type failure was fixed by explicitly typing valid JSON variants; extension-test typecheck and all 25 protocol-validator tests passed. The local full suite was not rerun merely to repeat passing work.

The prior published head `9fe8974589c5657ee79660a5e48de9c6ab84f368` also has a successful hosted CI check from [run 44182663362](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44182663362). Earlier Darwin tooling EPERM is not claimed as a code repair; current-head evidence above supersedes that prior-head CI result.

ClawSweeper also asks for installed-Gateway live discovery, turn completion and stable-upgrade evidence. Those flows were not performed. The native binary, separate HTTPS and direct old/new validator evidence support this scoped compatibility change, but do not prove live entitlement, a live GPT-6.2 turn, or a complete installed-Gateway upgrade. No such proof is claimed.

</details>

Credit: @VACInc reported the missing models and specified this upgrade and its regression coverage. @bdjben authored the catalog relay repair now landed in #197768; this PR builds on it and adds native discovery and cleanup proof.

After someone chose a folder on a paired device, New Session still showed an editable absolute path and a paragraph above the composer. On a phone it looked as if setup was unfinished, even though the folder was already selected.

User impact: once you choose a device folder, only its name stays in the workspace picker. Reopen the picker to change it. Canceling an edit keeps the previous selection. No migration or configuration change is needed.
